support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head catch
support_bodies.rationale: The flat underside of the -X rail's slide head - the Z seam's one down-looking face, and the whole of the screwless bottom-to-top joint's bearing against lift. Lifting a seated back-top lands its foot's flat top face on this one along the rail's whole run; pitching the catch would turn it into a cam and give that full-face bearing up. Its two interface islands are the one run either side of the PRV passage, the 12 mm opening that has to cross this flank, and that same opening is what lets the body root on the bed outside the flank instead of on the arm's own under-flare.

support_bodies.name: east Z-seam slide-head catch
support_bodies.rationale: The +X rail's slide head, the mirror of the west catch and continuous over its whole run because nothing crosses this flank. With no opening through the wall beside it the body has no lane to the bed, so it roots on the arm's own 45 degree under-flare 8.00 mm below the catch it carries. It and front-bottom's pair are the three material-rooted supports in the box and the only bodies outside the 15 mm band.

support_bodies.name: back-top service furniture and ceiling-dado tree
support_bodies.rationale: The two first contacts carry the west and east cold-core aft hold-down soffits over the core's insertion lane. Twenty-four later contacts branch from the same bed-rooted body through the open enclosure: the rear and west-wall service furniture, the drip-pan sleeve, nameplate and keystone roofs, both ASSE round-section soffits, all five power-row Wago roofs, the C14 aperture bridge, the three retained female-dado roof regions, the ASSE-local rail pocket roof, and the fixed-strip fore and relief soffits. The dado contacts are deliberately flat: a 6 mm upper flange closes the exterior over each 12 mm-square panel tongue, and their support withdraws through the groove's open Y-seam mouth before the panel slides in.

support_bodies.name: flow-regulator anchor outer end web
support_bodies.rationale: The outer end web of the -X wall rib closes around the flow regulator's round barrel seat and preserves its square retaining section. Its one support body establishes on the rib's lower solid and builds 22.32 mm before meeting this 6.0 x 2.4 mm contact.

support_bodies.name: water-split anchor outer end web
support_bodies.rationale: The outer end web of the -X wall rib closes around the water split's round barrel seat and preserves its square retaining section. Its one support body establishes on the rib's lower solid and builds 22.32 mm before meeting this 5.6 x 2.4 mm contact.

support_bodies.name: west lower Y-seam socket collar crown
support_bodies.rationale: The complete crown of the lower west Y-seam socket collar. It keeps the collar's full structural stock over the cross-pin's square slide slot and its blind heat-set pocket, so the pin registers on a square pass envelope and the M3 bears on a whole section; pitching the crown into a roof would erase that envelope. Its one tree grows from the bed through the open cavity.

support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head catch
support_bodies.rationale: The flat underside of the -X rail's slide head - the Z seam's one down-looking face, and the whole of the screwless bottom-to-top joint's bearing against lift. Lifting a seated front-top lands its foot's flat top face on this one along the rail's entire run, and pitching the catch would turn it into a cam. The arm under it already returns to the wall on a 45 degree under-flare, so there is no wall-rooted wedge left to grow, and nothing crosses this flank at the catch's height to give the body a lane to the bed: it roots on that under-flare 8.00 mm below the catch. It, its east mirror and back-bottom's east catch are the three material-rooted supports in the box and the only bodies outside the 15 mm band, and they are what the campaign owes its next fix.

support_bodies.name: collet-plate stop and pump-bay lintel tree
support_bodies.rationale: The lower contact carries the exact 1 mm flat land that stops the steel collet plate and defines its Z datum; its fore edge is already raked at 45 degrees. The upper contact is the lintel that closes the full-width removable pump-cartridge bay while carrying the display above it. A support-free gable across that deep opening would occupy the rectangular cartridge-withdrawal or display envelope. The two contacts share one long bed-rooted tree, so neither hides a separate short or material-rooted support.

support_bodies.name: west Y-seam ceiling-tongue socket crown
support_bodies.rationale: This flat is the complete crown of the upper west Y-seam socket collar, and the ceiling tongue rises directly from it. The crown preserves the socket's full registration web and gives the tongue its load-bearing root; its one removable tree grows from the bed through the open enclosure.

support_bodies.name: east Y-seam ceiling-tongue socket crown
support_bodies.rationale: This flat is the complete crown of the upper east Y-seam socket collar, and the ceiling tongue rises directly from it. support_bodies.name: X- pump boss-bearing shoulder
support_bodies.rationale: The flat annular shoulder bears axially on the fitted pump boss while the complete octagonal wall locates X, Y and yaw. Chamfering the shoulder would trade away bearing area rather than remove an accidental overhang; its centre bore remains open for direct support removal.
